ai.title: How I use AI
ai.intro: AI is part of how I build and part of what I build. It makes me faster; it does not lower the bar.

dremly.name: Dremly
dremly.line: Interprets a dream from text or voice, then turns it into an image or a short video.

posme.name: Posme
posme.line: Reads a single camera frame and designs a pose for that scene; live coaching runs on the phone.

rommer.name: Movement analysis for Rommer

ai.lead: I don't just prompt an assistant. I built my own Claude Code setup and keep training it on real projects.

spec.title: Spec first
spec.line: Every feature starts as a written spec and a task plan before any code is written.
spec.detail: My own Claude Code skills encode how I work: planning, handing a session over and picking it up again, motion rules for every interface.

agents.title: Agents as a team
agents.line: Coding agents build independent tasks in parallel, each in its own isolated branch.
agents.detail: I lead them like a team: clear briefs, the cheapest model that can do the job well, and a plain report of what was verified and what was not.

review.title: Independent review
review.line: Each task is checked against the spec and for quality by a separate reviewer, and I make the final call.
review.detail: Tools I wrote help me check: a click-to-inspect picker for web and mobile to point at the exact element, a verifier agent that runs the quality gate, a launcher that boots the emulator and the app.

gates.title: Gates, not trust
gates.line: Type checks, lint, unit and end-to-end tests have to pass before anything is merged or shipped.
gates.detail: When something fails silently, it becomes a written rule every agent reads. No internal detail reaches users, no production change happens without asking, and nothing is called verified until I have read the actual output.
